intake_title: Discontinuity of the Potts phase transition on Z^d for q >= 3, d >= 3
primary_source: Hugo Duminil-Copin, Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice (2017), Conjecture 2, printed p. 93 / PDF p. 92, https://www.unige.ch/~duminil/publi/2017PIMS.pdf
source_quote: Prove that the phase transition of the nearest-neighbor Potts model on Z^d (with d >= 3) is discontinuous for any q >= 3.
formalized_target: For every integer d >= 3 and integer q >= 3, the zero-field nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic q-state Potts model on Z^d has positive critical ordered magnetization: mu_{beta_c(d,q)}^{(i)}(sigma_0=i)>1/q for each color i.
scope_note: Conjecture 2 itself reports proofs for sufficiently high dimension at each fixed q>=3, sufficiently large q at each fixed d, and sufficiently spread-out interactions. The latter changes the nearest-neighbor model and does not settle C0048.
current_openness: UNKNOWN_AFTER_TARGETED_CHECK; no novelty or solved claim
recent_primary_check: 2018 Duminil-Copin ICM review arXiv:1712.04651 p.18 still calls the high-dimensional assertion conjectural; 2024 Gaite arXiv:2407.15497 and 2025 Yang et al. arXiv:2501.14320 are field-theory/finite-size studies, not a rigorous proof of the nearest-neighbor Z^3 target. Search is not a completeness certificate through 2026-10-10.

quantifier_warning: The integer-color Potts conjecture does not alone imply q_c(d)=2 for real FK weights. The cited 2018 ICM paper defines FK q>0 but does not define q_c(d) precisely in the cited paragraph. Existing card needs a scoped correction or a separately proved real-q bridge.
